areas_checked: Code moved during this review: crates/fx-basic/src/alternating.rs, crates/fx-basic/src/common.rs and crates/vixen-core/src/marks.rs were rewritten at 23:45:12 by another agent. All findings are against that version, re-read and re-run at 23:47. Two bugs I had found were fixed by that edit and are not reported. marks_in_range (start time only) became marks_inclusive_of_time, matching MarkCollection.MarksInclusiveOfTime, and the first-collection fallback now matches MarkCollectionSelectionService.Normalize at render time (its persistence gap is in alternating-10).

Owner's real uses: both are in Christmas Eve Sarajevo.tim, on Light Strip R (563 pixels) and Light Strip L (554 pixels), all 1117 FullColor. Parameters: TimeInterval, Interval=100, not static, GroupLevel=1, skip 1, no depth, default Red/Lime Flat100, span 5607 ms. Worked by hand and run through the Rust render on a 4-pixel stand-in with the same parameters: 57 intervals, each intent 99 ms, last one 5600-5699. The intents the two render paths produce agree; output would be identical, and none of the rendering findings touch these two effects. The overrun past 5607 ms is clipped the same way in both: ContextCurrentEffectsFull drops the effect after EndTime, and schedule.rs caps at effect_hi.

No C# was executed (dotnet is not installed here). C# results are hand-worked, or read from the existing tests/golden/Alternating.json. Rust results come from scratch programs in the session scratchpad, with their own CARGO_HOME and target directory. No repo files were edited by me; the file changes visible in the repo during the run came from other agents.

Rendering, worked by hand against C# and run in Rust: real parameters as above; static (one interval of TimeSpan-1 ms); mark overlapping the start (marks at 9800 lasting 450 ms, 10300, 10700, effect 10000-11000, R/L/B gives -200..299 L, 300..699 B, 700..999 R, matching C#); empty selection with marks at 300 and 700 (R, L, R); too-deep depth; GroupLevel 0; negative skip; overlapping targets; discrete with and without validate.

Rendering, compared line by line with no other differences: Math.Ceiling and Convert.ToInt32 of TotalMilliseconds/Interval, including Interval 0 and negative (dark in both); GroupBy against chunks partitioning and order; colour rotation with % for non-negative values; the interval minus 1 ms and <=0 guard; startTime advance in both modes; mark-relative times; PulseRenderer points, intent timing, zero-intensity skip and discrete path; Distinct on depth descent; EffectIntents.Add order. Rendering holds no state between renders.

No visible effect, so not reported: Rust TimeSpan::from_ms rounds to a tick where, as far as I recall, .NET truncates (I did not have the .NET source to confirm), at most 100 ns either way. Mark::new defaults to 500 ms where C# Mark is 450 ms, but it has no production caller yet (old marks use an explicit 450 at sequence.rs:834), and should be fixed before an editor creates marks. Curves with fewer than 2 points render at 100 in Rust where the C# comment says it throws; this comes from curve.rs and needs a damaged file.

Parameter table, all 10 rows against AlternatingData, Alternating attributes and the resource files: name, xml, kind, xml_ns and level, defaults (the whole constructor including Red and Lime with Flat100), categories and orders, labels, descriptions, property order, is_value, slider ranges, enum members and labels. Descriptor identity fields (GUID, author, version, description, group, data type and namespace, icon, info link) also match. Only the rows in alternating-3, -5, -7 and -8 differ.

Visibility: MarkCollectionId, EnableStatic, IntervalSkipCount and DepthOfEffect all match. Interval differs (alternating-4) and AlternatingMode is hidden (alternating-3). TargetPositioning is correctly hidden, since the C# never enables it.

Property setters: GroupLevel clamp (alternating-11), AlternatingMode normalization and MarkCollectionId name mapping (alternating-10), Colors re-validation (alternating-1). EnableStatic and EnableDepth setters only update attributes, which visibility covers. IsDirty, listeners and CheckLibraryReference were skipped per docs/PORTING_GUIDE.md.
Validation: the logic of validate matches CheckForInvalidColorData, including subset check, first valid colour, and curves left alone. The gap is that it is never called (alternating-1).

Custom thumbnails: the C# does not override GenerateVisualRepresentation or ForceGenerateVisualRepresentation, and Rust has force_visual false and visual None, so there is nothing to port. Thumbnails use the intent rasterizer in crates/vixen-session/src/thumbnail.rs.

Panics: no panic in 20 edge inputs run through the Rust render: no targets, single element, empty group, zero length in all three modes, 1 ms static, empty and None Colors, Interval 0 and negative, huge and negative GroupLevel, huge and negative depth, mixed depth, empty gradient and curve, one-point curve, duplicate marks.
V1 to V2 migration in crates/vixen-io/src/sequence_migrate.rs:248-279 matches TimedSequenceMigrator.cs:237-336, including the reversed colour order.
